title: Fix Time-Series Lens Top N truncation on partitioned dataset
summary: Root cause: load_slice(limit=500_000) used scanner.head() which on hive-partitioned datasets (by country) reads partitions alphabetically. The first 6 countries filled the 500k limit, causing the remaining 15 countries to be completely missing from grouped time-series aggregation. Fix: added limit=None support to load_slice (uses scanner.to_table() for unlimited scan) and changed query_grouped_time_series + _query_grouped_share_time_series to pass limit=None instead of 500_000.
backendChanges: parquet_repository.py: load_slice now supports limit=None to disable row truncation via scanner.to_table()
query_service.py: query_grouped_time_series and _query_grouped_share_time_series now pass limit=None for complete aggregation
risks: Unlimited scan on very large filtered datasets (>5M rows) could increase memory usage
Other load_slice callers with 200_000 limit may have similar partition-truncation risk for different query types
nextSteps: Deploy to server and verify Top 10 shows all countries
Consider applying same fix to other load_slice callers (200_000 limits)
Consider pushing group-by aggregation to PyArrow for better memory efficiency
